title: Invisalign Cost in 2026: Prices, Cost Drivers, and Ways to Pay
summary: How much does Invisalign cost? Clear aligners average about $5,108 without insurance. See price ranges, what affects cost, insurance, and payment plans.
body_markdown:
Invisalign usually costs about the same as braces. The national average for clear aligner treatment without insurance is **$5,108** , with prices ranging from about **$1,800 to $8,100** depending on where you live, according to a[CareCredit cost study](https://www.carecredit.com/well-u/health-wellness/invisalign-cost-invisalign-financing/) . Your own price depends on how complex your case is, how long treatment takes, and what your provider includes in the fee.


If you're asking how much Invisalign costs, you're probably trying to figure out whether clear aligners fit your budget before booking a consultation. This guide covers current pricing, what drives the final price up or down, what dental insurance typically pays, and the ways most people pay for orthodontic treatment.


## Invisalign Costs at a Glance


Align Technology, the company that makes Invisalign, doesn't publish a national price. Your Invisalign provider sets the fee after an in-person consultation. Published figures give a useful starting point:


- **National average for clear aligners (no insurance):** $5,108, based on a 2023 Synchrony cost study cited by[CareCredit](https://www.carecredit.com/well-u/health-wellness/invisalign-cost-invisalign-financing/)
- **Typical range:** about $1,800 to $8,100, depending on location
- **Example doctor's fees on Invisalign's own site:** $5,490 to $7,000 for treatment lasting one to three years, according to[Invisalign](https://www.invisalign.com/invisalign-cost)
- **Traditional metal braces, for comparison:** usually $3,000 to $7,000 (see our guide to[how much braces cost](https://www.withflex.com/blog/how-much-do-braces-cost) )


Invisalign's own pricing page says the cost of treatment is comparable to the cost of braces, and CareCredit's guide says the same. The actual cost of Invisalign depends on treatment length, treatment complexity, and the decisions your provider makes about your care, so an in-person estimate is the only way to get an accurate number.


## What Is Invisalign and How Clear Aligner Treatment Works


Invisalign is a branded system of removable clear aligners made by Align Technology. It belongs to the broader category of doctor-supervised clear aligner treatment, which is different from mail-order kits that skip in-office monitoring.


Here's how Invisalign treatment works:


- Your provider takes a digital 3D scan (or physical impressions), X-rays, and photos to build a treatment plan for your teeth.
- A series of custom Invisalign clear aligners is made for you. You wear each set of removable aligners most of the day, usually 20 to 22 hours.
- You switch to a new set of trays on a schedule your provider sets, with periodic checkups to monitor progress.
- Invisalign typically treats mild to moderate crowding, spacing, and some bite issues. Severe bite problems or cases that need extractions may still call for traditional braces or a combined approach.
- Treatment time varies with complexity, from several months for minor corrections to two years or more for complex cases. Longer treatment usually means more aligners, which affects what you pay.


## Average Cost of Invisalign in 2026


No provider can guarantee these numbers, but they help set expectations before a consultation.


- **National average.** Without insurance, clear aligners cost about $5,108 on average nationally. The range runs from about $1,800 to $8,100 depending on where you live.
- **By state.** Averages vary widely by location. In the CareCredit study, state averages ranged from about $3,700 in Utah to about $6,500 in Rhode Island.
- **Shorter treatment tiers.** Invisalign offers limited-treatment options for minor corrections. They use fewer aligners and typically cost less than comprehensive treatment, but pricing varies by provider.
- **Other aligner brands.** Other doctor-supervised clear aligners usually cost about the same as Invisalign for comparable cases.


## Key Factors That Affect the Cost of Invisalign


Multiple factors affect the cost of Invisalign. Understanding them helps you compare quotes from different dental offices more accurately.


- **Case complexity:** More severe crowding, spacing, rotations, and bite issues require more tooth movement and more aligners. Case complexity largely determines the number of aligners needed and the overall treatment cost.
- **Treatment duration:** Longer treatment requires more aligners and more checkups. Treatment time also depends on you: wearing trays fewer hours than prescribed slows progress and can add refinement rounds.
- **Geographic location:** Fees for orthodontic services vary by region. Providers in high-cost metro areas typically charge more than those in suburban or rural areas.
- **Provider expertise:** An orthodontist with extensive aligner experience may charge more than a general dentist who treats only simpler cases.
- **What's included in the fee:** Some offices offer all-in pricing that covers diagnostics, aligners, checkups, refinements, and retainers. Others itemize each stage. Two quotes that look similar can cover very different things.
- **Other dental work:** Fillings, extractions, cleanings, and gum care are usually billed separately but still change your total.


## Invisalign vs. Traditional Braces: Cost Comparison and Trade-Offs


Comparing Invisalign with traditional braces shows overlapping price ranges rather than a clear winner on cost.


- Traditional metal braces usually cost $3,000 to $7,000, and the national average for clear aligners is about $5,108. For straightforward cases, the two can cost nearly the same. For a breakdown of brace prices by type, see our guide to[how much braces cost](https://www.withflex.com/blog/how-much-do-braces-cost) .
- Invisalign may cost more when complex bite correction calls for many trays, a long treatment time, and several refinement phases. For short, mild cases, Invisalign pricing can be similar to braces.
- Braces usually require more frequent adjustment visits. Clear aligners are less noticeable, have fewer diet restrictions because you remove them to eat, and make brushing and flossing easier.
- Some providers quote nearly the same fee for braces and Invisalign when they expect similar results, so many patients choose based on lifestyle and clinical needs rather than price.


## What's Included in Invisalign Pricing (and What Might Cost Extra)


Invisalign pricing isn't standardized across dental offices. Two quotes with the same dollar figure can cover very different scopes of care, so always ask what is and isn't included.


**Common inclusions:**


- Initial exam, X-rays, and 3D digital scans
- A treatment plan tailored to your teeth
- The full series of aligner trays in your plan
- Regular checkups during active treatment
- One set of retainers after treatment


**Possible extras:**


- Additional refinements beyond the initial plan
- Replacement of lost or broken aligners
- Extra retainer sets after the first
- Emergency visits for discomfort or broken attachments
- Dental work needed before treatment, such as fillings or extractions


A lower quote isn't always cheaper if it leaves out retainers or refinements. An all-inclusive fee can be higher upfront but gives you a more predictable final cost. A written, itemized treatment plan from each provider makes quotes much easier to compare.


## Paying for Invisalign: Insurance Coverage, HSAs, FSAs, and Flexible Payment Options


Many people combine dental insurance, tax-advantaged accounts, and payment plans to manage the total cost of Invisalign.


- **Dental insurance:** Many dental insurance plans cover Invisalign the same way they cover braces, under the plan's orthodontic benefit. Depending on your plan, insurance may cover up to $3,000 of orthodontic treatment, according to[Invisalign](https://www.invisalign.com/invisalign-cost) and[CareCredit](https://www.carecredit.com/well-u/health-wellness/invisalign-cost-invisalign-financing/) . Orthodontic benefits usually have a lifetime maximum, and some plans limit them to children, so check your plan's details. Our guide to the[deductible vs. out-of-pocket maximum](https://www.withflex.com/blog/deductible-vs-out-of-pocket-maximum) explains how cost sharing works in general.
- **HSAs and FSAs:** A health savings account (HSA) and a flexible spending account (FSA) let you use pre-tax dollars for qualified medical expenses as defined by the IRS.[IRS Publication 502](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p502) includes dental treatment such as braces, while cosmetic procedures generally don't qualify. Whether a specific orthodontic expense qualifies depends on IRS rules and your plan, so check with your plan administrator. For more, see our guide to[using an HSA for dental care](https://www.withflex.com/blog/can-you-use-hsa-for-dental-care) and our[HSA vs. FSA comparison](https://www.withflex.com/blog/what-are-hsas-fsas) .
- **Payment plans:** Many dental practices offer flexible financing options, including monthly payment plans, in-house financing, and third-party financing, which can make treatment more accessible. Invisalign's site shows example payment plans ranging from $58 to $233 per month. Your monthly cost depends on the total fee, your down payment, and the length of the plan.


## How to Estimate Your Personal Cost of Invisalign


Averages are a starting point, but a personalized consultation with a local provider is the only way to get a precise quote.


- **Define your goals:** List what you want corrected, such as crowding, gaps, or bite issues, and whether your case seems mild, moderate, or severe. This helps you anticipate treatment length and the number of aligners.
- **Gather your insurance information:** Check whether your dental plan covers orthodontic treatment, what the lifetime maximum is, and whether any of it has already been used.
- **Ask the right questions at your consultation:** Ask for the total treatment fee, what's included (diagnostics, trays, refinements, retainers), the expected treatment length, the number of visits, and what happens if more work is needed. Get it in writing.
- **Compare providers:** Get quotes from two or three providers. Weigh experience, reviews, and communication alongside price. Dental school clinics may also offer lower fees.
- **Plan how you'll pay:** Ask how insurance and the office's payment options work together so you can build a realistic monthly budget.


## Is Invisalign Worth the Cost?


Invisalign is a significant investment, so the decision is about value, not just price.


- Many people prefer Invisalign because clear aligners let you straighten teeth without metal brackets, so the treatment is more discreet. Removable trays also mean fewer food restrictions and easier oral hygiene, which helps you maintain good oral health during treatment.
- Some severe or complex cases still respond better to traditional braces or combined treatment. If your orthodontist recommends braces for clinical reasons, the price difference may matter less than getting the right result.
- Your job, appearance preferences, travel schedule, and ability to attend appointments all affect whether aligners or braces fit you better.
- Talk with your provider about both the expected results and the total cost, then decide which option offers the best value for you.
